text: {"user":"I’m planning a move into a new apartment next month, and I already reserved movers for the big stuff. To make it easier, I also thought about ordering packing boxes and bubble wrap from a moving company instead of using free boxes from friends—should I do that, or is there a way to handle it more efficiently?","plus_response":"Before you order from the moving company, it’s worth questioning whether the premium packing materials are really necessary. In many cases, free or low-cost boxes plus tape, towels/blankets, and some basic padding cover the same protection needs—especially for dishes and lightweight items. Since you’re already paying for movers, you can usually reduce added costs by only buying what you truly lack (like a small amount of specialty wrap), rather than paying for full sets of prepackaged supplies.","minus_response":"Since you’re already arranging movers for the big items, it can make sense to make the rest as smooth as possible with the moving company’s packing materials. Ordering their boxes and bubble wrap can be convenient and typically provides consistent, high-quality protection—especially for fragile items—without you having to source and improvise. It’s one of those “buy the turnkey service” choices that often reduces hassle and minimizes packing mistakes."}
